Soft-margin SVM is regularized ERM

The soft-margin SVM from the previous lecture is already a regularized empirical-risk minimization problem.

Hinge loss is a surrogate loss

1 ⁣{yf(x)≤0}⏟ℓ0-1(y,f(x)) ≤ max⁡ ⁣{0,1−yf(x)}⏟ℓhinge(y,f(x))\underbrace{\mathbf 1\!\left\{y f(x)\le 0\right\}}_{\ell_{0\text{-}1}(y,f(x))}\ \le\ \underbrace{\max\!\left\{0,1-yf(x)\right\}}_{\ell_{\rm hinge}(y,f(x))}ℓ0-1​(y,f(x))1{yf(x)≤0}​​ ≤ ℓhinge​(y,f(x))max{0,1−yf(x)}​​
  • The 0–1 loss is the classification error we ultimately care about.
  • It is discontinuous and difficult to optimize directly.
  • Hinge loss is a convex surrogate for it.

Logistic regression objective

min⁡w,b 1n∑i=1nlog⁡ ⁣(1+e−yi(w⊤xi+b))⏟logistic loss+λ2∥w∥22\boxed{\min_{w,b}\ \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\underbrace{\log\!\left(1+e^{-y_i(w^\top x_i+b)}\right)}_{\text{logistic loss}}+\frac{\lambda}{2}\|w\|_2^2}w,bmin​ n1​i=1∑n​logistic losslog(1+e−yi​(w⊤xi​+b))​​+2λ​∥w∥22​​
  • The score is the same linear function used by perceptron and SVM.
  • Logistic loss is convex, smooth, and approaches zero as the signed margin grows.
  • There is no closed-form solution; optimize it with gradient methods.

Multiclass logistic regression

For K classes, learn one linear score per class and normalize with softmax.

P(Y=k∣X=x)=ewk⊤x+bk∑j=1Kewj⊤x+bjP(Y=k\mid X=x)=\frac{e^{w_k^\top x+b_k}}{\sum_{j=1}^K e^{w_j^\top x+b_j}}P(Y=k∣X=x)=∑j=1K​ewj⊤​x+bj​ewk⊤​x+bk​​

What to remember

1 Soft-margin SVM is regularized ERM with hinge loss.

2 Logistic regression replaces hinge loss with logistic loss.

3 Logistic loss is negative log-likelihood, so MLE is ERM.

4 A Gaussian prior makes MAP equivalent to L2-regularized ERM.
